### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via config_change (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_CHANGE_ACTION; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via SettingsAuditSink (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsAuditSink (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/settings-service.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class), setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SettingsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via setMany (symbol, a method of class SettingsService))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via config_change (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_CHANGE_ACTION; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via config_change (literal, a string literal in CONFIG_CHANGE_ACTION; a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f2ddf8d699b432b2ad5b9dbb0c8130d575477965` — the merge of head `47b9abc5b704afcd6d9439c4c6cb9af6b96a68c9` into base `26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f2ddf8d699b432b2ad5b9dbb0c8130d575477965 && git checkout f2ddf8d699b432b2ad5b9dbb0c8130d575477965
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383 47b9abc5b704afcd6d9439c4c6cb9af6b96a68c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383 && git merge --no-ff 47b9abc5b704afcd6d9439c4c6cb9af6b96a68c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 26c965cb8f61ca59804d55e27e737bf7ff91b383` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `47b9abc5b704afcd6d9439c4c6cb9af6b96a68c9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-settings/src/config-change-audit.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-field-redaction.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/config-change-audit.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-field-redaction.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/settings-config-change-audit.dogfood.test.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/platform-core.json, .changeset/30923-config-change-before-after.md + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/served-fields.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-log.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-setting.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-platform-setting.object.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, docs/adr/0007-settings-manifest-and-kv-store.md, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/CHANGELOG.md (precedent entries fbcc05f and 2ecf6a7)

Face note: `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the nine changed paths decides no schema or governed face. The owed face is the declaration face (`Clause-②: yes` alone). This record is served at the higher tier as asked; a tier above the owed one is allowed (contract-review.md: the tier is not a ceiling).

### ① Derived judgments

**Must-fix: none.**

**Should-fix (follow-up cards, not blockers; both outside the claim's file surface):**

- S1. `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts:277-279` still says a `config_change` row's "digest sits next to the mirror's row that carries the value". True for a secret key only now. The dev noted it in the PR body. One comment line; file a docs-only follow-up.
- S2. `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts:51-58` says a `config_change` row that names no `record_id` carries no record's field values. After this PR such a row (only when the store hands back no id, `settings-service.ts:3932-3937`) carries a readable non-secret value. The field redaction still narrows it, because it keys on `object_name` and not on `record_id` (`audit-log-field-redaction.ts:182-184`), so the behaviour is right and only the comment is stale. Same follow-up as S1.

**Confirmed, by file and line:**

1. Secret rule, one place. `settings-service.ts:3820-3822` `auditReadable(keyIsSecret, row)` answers true only when the key is not in `encryptedKeys` and the row is not stored `encrypted: true`. `encryptedKeys` is filled at `settings-service.ts:1259` from the manifest's `encrypted` or `type: 'password'`. The after side is handed to the sink only under `!isNull && auditReadable(isEncrypted, null)` (`settings-service.ts:2909`); the before side goes through `auditPrevious` (`settings-service.ts:3847-3863`), which returns a readable value only when `auditReadable(keyIsSecret, previous)` holds for the previous row itself. So:
   - set of a secret: no `value`, `valueDigest` is the masked keyed digest (`:2906`, `:3829-3830`); old side is the keyed `old_hash` (`:2879-2883`, `previousSecretAuditDigest` `:3902-3924`, plaintext lives in that frame only and is never logged).
   - reset of a secret: `new_value` is `null` (`config-change-audit.ts:347`); `old_value` carries the masked keyed digest only.
   - first write: `previous` is `null` from `upsertRow` (`settings-service.ts:3983`, `:3995`) so `old_value` is `null`.
   - key flipped to secret after a plaintext write: `auditReadable(true, prevPlainRow)` is false; `oldHash` from `previousSecretAuditDigest` is `null` because `previous.encrypted !== true` (`:3907`); result is the bare placeholder, no value, no unkeyed hash (`:3863`). Pinned at `config-change-audit.test.ts:1009-1029`.
   - key flipped from secret to plain: previous row is stored `encrypted: true`, so `auditReadable(false, prevEncRow)` is false; the comment at `:3861-3862` is right that a non-secret key's `oldHash` is unkeyed and so is not used; result is the bare placeholder. Pinned at `:1031-1045`, with `not.toHaveProperty('value')` at `:1042`.
   - unknown key not in any manifest: `setMany` refuses the whole call with `UnknownKeyError` before any write (`settings-service.ts:2087`), so no row is written. Fail closed.
   - `metadata` is unchanged and carries `event, namespace, key, scope, encrypted, requestId` only (`config-change-audit.ts:365-372`).
   - No log line or error carries a value: the sink's one error message carries the engine's `err.message` (`config-change-audit.ts:383-400`), and the row it tried to insert never holds a secret's plaintext; `previousSecretAuditDigest`'s warn line carries the decrypt error only (`settings-service.ts:3916-3919`).
2. Doors. `this.audit.record(...)` has one caller, `setMany` (`settings-service.ts:2897`). `set` (`:2613`) and `resetNamespace` (`:3452`) go through it. `sys_setting` and `sys_platform_setting` declare `managedBy: 'engine-owned'` and `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']` (`sys-setting.object.ts:48`, `:259`; `sys-platform-setting.object.ts:53`, `:147`), so the data API cannot write them. The CLI ownership-apply and the metadata-protocol migrations touch the stores' identity columns, not values, and write no `config_change` row.
3. Redaction. `audit-log-field-redaction.ts:182-185` treats a row as a settings change when `action === 'config_change'` and `object_name` is in `AUDIT_LOG_SETTINGS_STORE_OBJECTS`, which is `[sys_setting, sys_platform_setting]` (`sys-audit-log.object.ts:60-63`), so tenant/user scope and global scope are both keyed. The served set comes from the same `servedFor(object)` the CRUD mirror's rows use (`:192-193`, `servedFieldsPerRead` in `served-fields.ts:100`; readable intersected with queryable, fail-closed to `[]` when the mask cannot be answered, `served-fields.ts:85-93`). The settings branch differs only in the drop function: `dropUnservedSettingValue` (`:140-150`) removes `value` and `digest` on both columns when `value` is not served, and keeps `namespace`, `key`, `scope`. A digest of a non-secret value is an unkeyed SHA-256 (`settings-service.ts:2853`), so dropping it with the value is the right call for a low-entropy value. A non-object snapshot is dropped (`:205-208`). Rows of other actions, and a `config_change` row naming no settings store, hit `continue` at `:185` and are served as written. Readers served `value` get the bytes unchanged (`:209-213`).
4. Predicate probing of the now-readable `new_value` is already closed: `parent-field-query-guard.ts` refuses a non-system query naming `old_value`/`new_value` for a reader withheld any field of the parent object the query names (or of every registered object when it names none), and it does not condition on `action`, so `config_change` rows are inside its class.
5. The changeset body states the narrowed case in words (the masked reader gets neither value nor digest), so an upgrading reader who greps the ledger entry finds it.
6. ADR-0007 § Audit & history (`docs/adr/0007-settings-manifest-and-kv-store.md:338-344`) asks for before and after on `sys_audit_log`, and for an encrypted value only a placeholder plus checksum. The row now carries both sides, and a secret's sides carry the placeholder with the keyed checksum. The PR implements the ADR; the old module header was the deviation.
7. QA checklist `platform-core.json`: `source[1]` rewritten, revision 5 to 6 with a dated history row (`:3329`, `:3411`, `:3448-3453`). Every clause there scores the secret `mail.api_key`, whose rows still carry the masked digest only, so no clause moves. Right.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-settings: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch`. Correct. Metadata-protocol is `none` (no spec key, no authorable value, no default moves; the only type change is two optional fields on `SettingsAuditSink.record`'s entry, `settings-service.types.ts:262-284`, exported via `index.ts:69`, which a host sink may ignore). AGENTS.md step 3: `none` takes `patch`.

Clause-② arm: `yes (widening)` stands. Reasoning against the repo's own precedent on this ledger:
- fbcc05f (#21155, the original snapshot redaction on the same seam) took the value away from a reader whose field-level security already masked the field, and was landed as a non-breaking `Clause-②: no`, on the ground that ledger readers are not field-unrestricted by default.
- 2ecf6a7 (#26750) took whole rows away from readers regardless of their own field mask, and was `no (narrowing)` with the BREAKING banner.
- This PR's plugin-audit half is the first kind: the only reader who loses anything is one whose security answer already withholds the settings store's `value`, and what they lose is a derivative of that field (an unkeyed digest a dictionary search inverts). Nothing is taken from a reader served the field, no export or key is removed, and the row shape for a secret is byte-identical to before (pinned at `config-change-audit.test.ts:1006`). The widening half (the readable value, the two optional sink fields) is real and reaches every served reader. So `yes (widening)` is the right single arm; `no (narrowing)` would overstate a mask enforcement the repo has not treated as breaking before. Answer to the dev's open question: option A.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev's open question on the Clause-② arm: answered above, A.
- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (read from the API), so no author note is owed under contract-review.md.
- PR body's `Verification` quotes local runs on the final head; this record did not re-run them. Check-runs on the head read from the API: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core 1-8 and aggregate, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate all `completed/success`; UI lint/typecheck/build skipped (no `ui/` paths).
- The two stale comments (S1, S2) sit outside the claim's file surface; they are follow-up cards, not reasons to hold this head.

### ④ Design judgment

Declaration face only: no schema or governed path in the diff, no narrowing arm declared, so ④ is not owed. For the record, the one design call made here is read against ADR-0007: the before-side describes the stored row at the write's own rung (the row `record_id` names), so a first tenant-scope write records a null before even when a global value or the default was in force. That is the ADR's "before" for the row the ledger points at, and it matches what `old_hash` has always fingerprinted. Consistent.

Tests, read for what they pin and whether the reported ablations go red:
- Secret rule: `config-change-audit.test.ts:979-1007` asserts no plaintext in `old_value`, `new_value` or `metadata` across set, rotate and reset, that every side is the encrypted marker around a 64-hex keyed digest, and that `new_value` keys are unchanged. Ablation A (`auditReadable` returns true) puts `value` on the after side, so `not.toHaveProperty('value')` goes red; the flip case at `:1009-1029` would carry the old plaintext in `old_value`, red; the unflip case at `:1031-1045` would carry `value: null` on the old side, red on `not.toHaveProperty('value')`. The three readable cases do not touch the rule, green. Matches the report.
- Reset and first write: `:926-944` (first write null before, change readable both sides, before digest equals previous after digest and the trail's `old_hash`), `:963-977` (reset records its before, null after; the write after a reset records a null before).
- Redaction: `audit-log-field-redaction.test.ts:371-432`. The masked cases use `toEqual(WHICH)`, which fails if `digest` survives, so "neither value nor digest" is pinned on both stores. Ablation B (the `config_change` branch removed from the guard at `:182-185`) makes the row hit `continue`, so both masked cases keep the value, red; the non-JSON case is served as written, red; control and no-store cases pass either way. Matches the report.
- The dogfood pin and the route case (`:946-961`) cover the PUT door.
